newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices fall five percent at New Zealand sales.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices fall five percent at New Zealand sales.

text.p: Wool prices generally fell by five percent at wool sales in Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The provisional segment indicators compared with last week's sales (in cents per kg clean) were:
Market - 421, down 25; medium - 467, down 43; strong - 386, down 21; lamb - 363, down 21.
There were 5,194 tonnes on offer of which 37 percent was passed in. Crossbred fleece comprised 49 percent of the offering and second shear 23 percent.

Crossbred fleece 32-35 micron was 3.0 percent cheaper while 36 micron and stronger was 4.0 to 6.0 percent cheaper. Cotts was 6.0 to 7.0 percent cheaper, second shear was 2.5 to 5.0 percent cheaper and first lambs were 3.0 to 5.0 percent cheaper.
Bulky skirtings were 5.0 to 7.5 percent cheaper and second shear bellies and pieces were 5.0 to 10 percent cheaper.
Principal interest came from Western Europe, China, and the local mills, with support from Turkey, Nepal, the United States, India and Australia. The next sales are on January 16.
